images.title: Four thirds as whole plus part
images.purpose: Show that four scoops of 1/3 packet fill one packet with one scoop over, so 4/3 is written as 1 + 1/3.
images.composition: Two equal horizontal packet bars stacked with space between them, a brace under the full one, and one equation on the right.
images.exact_structure: Two identical horizontal bars standing for 2 packets, each split by thin grey #6B7280 lines into exactly 3 equal parts. Top bar: all 3 parts filled teal #0072B2, with a brace underneath. Bottom bar, directly below and left aligned: the first part filled amber #E69F00, the other 2 parts empty outline. To the right, one line of equation text. Exactly 2 bars, 6 parts, 4 filled.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
bars of different lengths, or thirds that are not equal
images.takeaway: Four thirds is one whole plus one third.
images.description: A full packet bar of 3 teal thirds braced as 1 packet, and a second bar with 1 amber third labelled 1/3; beside them, 4/3 = 1 + 1/3.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say the full bar as the whole and the amber part as what comes after the plus.

image_decisions.why: A full bar and a partly filled bar show the whole plus part split in one glance.
